description: The plot illustrates how accuracy metrics vary with initial confidence by showing three series (final accuracy, initial accuracy, and their difference) across discrete initial-confidence values. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and shows tick labels from 0.71 to 1.00 (irregularly spaced discrete values, including 0.71, 0.73, 0.79, 0.82–0.87, and 0.90–1.00). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced ticks at 0.2 intervals. The “Final Accuracy” line is blue with circular markers and a solid line with vertical error bars; it starts near 0.90 at 0.71, dips to about 0.73 at 0.73, rises to about 0.98 at 0.79, and then stays mostly in the high 0.8–0.9 range through 1.00, with visible local highs around 0.91 and 0.96–0.97 (near ~0.98) and ending near ~0.96 at 1.00. The “Δ Accuracy” line is orange with diamond markers and a dashed line with error bars; it begins around 0.36 at 0.71, drops to about 0.10 at 0.73, remains near ~0.08–0.30 across most mid-range confidences, shows a pronounced spike around 0.87 at roughly 0.45, dips near 0.90 to about 0.04, has additional higher points around 0.91 (~0.41) and 0.94 (~0.45), and ends near ~0.08 at 1.00. The “Initial Accuracy” line is green with square markers and a dash-dot line with error bars; it starts near 0.55 at 0.71, increases to about 0.63 at 0.73 and about 0.90 at 0.79, drops to roughly 0.65–0.75 across 0.82–0.86, falls to about 0.45 at 0.87, rises to about 0.82 at 0.90, fluctuates between roughly 0.58 and 0.82 from 0.91 to 0.99, and ends near ~0.90 at 1.00.
